content.title: About
content.content: A sweet roll without frosting is a soft sponge roll soaked with fragrant syrup and filled with a light cream or fruit purée. It has no icing, which keeps the texture airy and the flavor pure.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The roll tradition began in Europe in the 19th century and quickly spread worldwide.
Sweet rolls are a popular treat for birthdays, holidays, and celebrations.
Skipping the frosting makes the roll easier to prepare and helps control sugar levels.
Fillings can range from berry, nut, chocolate to creamy cheese variations.
The roll can be sliced thinly and served as bite‑size desserts.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The sponge cake provides carbohydrates that supply quick energy.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Creamy fillings often use cottage cheese, yogurt, or eggs, adding protein.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Flour and eggs are rich in B1, B2, and B6 vitamins, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: Depending on the filling, the roll can provide calcium, magnesium, and potassium.

items.title: Moderate fat level
items.content: When the filling is made with low‑fat dairy, the overall fat content remains modest.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional sponge cake uses wheat flour, which is unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Syrup and sweet fillings raise sugar levels, so those with diabetes should limit portions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Even without frosting, the roll remains calorie‑dense due to the cake and cream.

items.title: Food intolerances
items.content: Fillings may contain dairy, nuts, or eggs, which can trigger allergies.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the roll in individual slices, optionally dusted with powdered sugar or fresh berries. It can be eaten with hands or using a knife and fork.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the roll in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, refrigerate up to 5 days or freeze for up to 2 months.
